body:
m1 - BLOCK CLEARED, corrected head SHA is 1b51be9 on m1/resolution. Re-gate whenever you are ready.

FULL STACK, in order: c1049f2, e538a09, 2adfff2, aee72ed, 4383a85, 02840a9, a9fd20f, 1b51be9.

GATE ON THE MERGED TREE, every module that constructs a RecallGraph plus cross-platform, exit 0 on all:
  recall 41, align 179, interview 81, codec 98, embedBench 52, fixtures 110, laws 81
  alignJS 179, alignNative 179, codecJS 98
  scalafmtCheckAll clean, run as the last action before commit.

WHAT 1b51be9 CONTAINS - two breakages from two different commits, not one:

codec, broken by 4383a85. I fixed the FIXTURE, not the law. The segmenter produces text including terminal punctuation, which is why five modules passed unchanged; the hand-written codec fixture was the incoherent object the law forbids. Weakening the comparison would have made the fixture legal by making the guarantee meaningless. No encoded-JSON expectation moved - the round-trips derive from the fixture, not from pinned literals, so there was no golden-style re-cut to authorise.

embed-bench, broken by a9fd20f. I did NOT take the one-character `.value` fix. It would have compiled in thirty seconds and stripped the support I had spent the previous commit adding, at the artifact that publishes clocks - your SignatureProjection block, reproduced by me under time pressure. ClockPanel carries the support now, rendered discourse=0.047@0.256. StepMass gained a `support` accessor so both carriers answer that question through the same word.

THREE THINGS I OWE YOU PLAINLY, none of which you asked for:

1. Your "everything else in the merged tree is clean" was not established - your run aborted at compile with 17 errors, so it never reached codec, and codec's failure is a RUNTIME initializer error that no compile error would surface. I sent this separately; repeating it here so it is attached to the SHA you gate.

2. Rule 3's count is wrong. THREE modules reference RecallSignature, not two: align (6 files), embed-bench (1), fixtures (WarOfTheGhostsAlignmentSuite.scala:423). Mine covered fixtures by luck of habit. If the rule ships saying "two", the next migrator breaks that suite - and it is test-only, so it fails at runtime and hides behind any compile error, exactly as codec did. I would drop the number from the rule entirely; a count in a rule is a fact that was true once.

3. My own phrase "the seven RecallGraph modules" has the same defect and I would not put it in governance either. It was seven when I counted it.

I also released two reservations I turned out not to need - MetricsSuite and LeakageSuite - once defaulting ClockPanel's support parameter meant their call sites compiled untouched. Third time tonight I have had to think about my own orphaned holds, so I am now checking in-flight after every commit rather than after every bead.
